stem.en: Kabir says a tape made of two kinds of letter "is half as good as one with four". For a twelve-letter tape, what is the real ratio of possible messages?

text.en: Four kinds gives about four thousand times more messages than two kinds: seventeen million against four thousand. Each extra choice per position multiplies, not adds.

feedback.en: At every one of twelve positions, two choices against four. That is two to the twelfth against four to the twelfth, and the gap is four thousand times.
True, but the tape must be twice as long. At the same length, two letters spell far fewer things.
Two is enough for difference. Computers run on two. Two kinds of letter is a real alphabet, only a smaller one.

explanation.en: Possibilities multiply along the tape. Kinds of letter raised to the power of the length. Small changes in the base make huge changes in the total.
